newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: Zimbabwe government vows tough stance on strike.
newsitem.headline: Zimbabwe government vows tough stance on strike.

text.p: The Zimbabwean government vowed on Friday to maintain a tough stance against striking doctors and nurses, saying they were solely to blame for crippling the country's public health system.

Acting Public Service, Labour and Social Welfare Minister Nathan Shaumyarira told state media that President Robert Mugabe's government -- which has come under intense pressure to resolve the strike -- would not reverse its decision to fire all using strikes to press demands for higher pay and better working conditions.
An estimated 10,000 nurses have been on strike since October 21, and they were joined this week by doctors who were angry at the arrest of two union colleagues accused of inciting the strike.

Doctors Farai Jiah and Austin Bene -- both leaders of the state Hospitals Doctors Association -- were freed on Wednesday by a Harare court which said it needed time to decide whether to refer their case to the Supreme Court as their lawyer had raised constitutional issues during an initial remand hearing.

But the doctors, and other medical staff mainly at Zimbabwe's two largest hospitals, have stayed on the streets with the nurses, saying they will only resume work when the government addresses their pay demands and reinstates those fired.

"We are standing firm on our principles that doctors and nurses should not use the strike as a weapon. That door is closed and it is not going to be useful because they will get nothing in the area of the strike," Shamuyarira said.
The two Harare hospitals -- Harare and Parirenyatwa -- were closed on Wednesday, placing heavy pressure on municipal clinics and private surgeries.
